1977.title: A late-season arrival.
1977.story: Villeneuve joined Ferrari for the last two races after Lauda’s departure. At Fuji, a collision with Peterson’s Tyrrell sent his car off the track; a marshal and a photographer standing in a prohibited area were killed.

1978.title: Victory at home.
1978.story: Villeneuve’s first full season brought third place in Austria. At the final round, on the new Montreal circuit, he won his home Grand Prix, the first Formula One victory for a Canadian driver.

1979.title: Runner-up by four points.
1979.story: Three wins, at Kyalami, Long Beach and Watkins Glen, and seven podium finishes. Villeneuve followed Scheckter home at Monza and finished the season runner-up, four points behind his team-mate.

1980.title: A difficult year in the T5.
1980.story: The 312 T5 had only partial ground effects, and Villeneuve scored six points all season. Two fifth places, at Monaco and in Canada, were his best results.

1981.title: Turbo power, two wins.
1981.story: The turbocharged 126 CK was powerful but difficult to handle. Villeneuve still won at Monaco and at Jarama, where he held off four cars, then took third in the rain in Canada.

1982.title: A season cut short.
1982.story: Villeneuve finished second at Imola after Pironi passed him on the final lap, against what he understood as team orders. Two weeks later, he was killed in final qualifying at Zolder.

1979.title: Champion at Monza.
1979.story: Wins in Belgium, Monaco and Italy brought Scheckter the drivers’ title, sealed at Monza with Villeneuve following him home. Ferrari would wait 21 years for its next drivers’ champion.

1980.title: The champion steps away.
1980.story: In the 312 T5, Scheckter scored only two points and failed to qualify in Canada. The reigning champion retired from Formula One at the end of the season.

1989.title: A winning debut in red.
1989.story: Mansell won on his Ferrari debut in Brazil and again in Hungary, from 12th on the grid. Disqualifications in Canada and Portugal marked a season that ended fourth in the championship.

1990.title: One win in Portugal.
1990.story: Mansell won from pole position in Portugal, his only victory of the season, among five podium finishes. He finished fifth in the championship as team-mate Prost fought Senna for the title.

1990.title: Decided at the first corner.
1990.story: Five wins, including Ferrari’s 100th Grand Prix victory in France, carried Prost into a title fight with Senna. It ended in a first-corner collision at Suzuka; Prost finished runner-up, seven points behind.

1991.title: A partnership ends early.
1991.story: Five podium finishes, but no victories, from the 642 and its successor, the 643. After publicly criticising the car, Prost was dismissed before the final race in Australia.

2007.title: One point, one title.
2007.story: Räikkönen won on his Ferrari debut in Australia and took six victories in all. Seven points behind Hamilton before the final race, he won in Brazil to claim the title by one point.

2008.title: Early wins, team honours.
2008.story: Wins in Malaysia and Spain came early in a season of nine podium finishes. Räikkönen finished third in the drivers’ standings as Ferrari won the constructors’ championship.

2009.title: A lone win at Spa.
2009.story: After no points from the first three races, Räikkönen won from sixth on the grid at Spa, Ferrari’s only victory of the year. Ferrari then bought out his contract’s final year to make way for Alonso.

2014.title: A difficult return.
2014.story: Räikkönen rejoined Ferrari alongside Alonso for the first season of hybrid turbo power. He did not reach the podium; fourth in Belgium was his best result, and he finished 12th in the standings.

2015.title: Alongside a new team-mate.
2015.story: Second place in Bahrain was the first of three podiums in Räikkönen’s first season alongside Vettel. Third places in Singapore and Abu Dhabi followed, and he finished fourth in the championship.

2016.title: Consistency without victory.
2016.story: Second places in Bahrain and Spain, and third places in Russia and Austria, made four podium finishes for Räikkönen. A first win since his return remained out of reach.

2017.title: Pole at Monaco.
2017.story: Pole position at Monaco, his first since 2008, led to second place behind Vettel. Six more podium finishes followed, including second in Hungary, but a victory remained out of reach.

2018.title: A final win in red.
2018.story: Räikkönen’s Monza pole was then the fastest lap in Formula One history, and he won in Austin, his first victory since 2013. Twelve podiums brought third in the championship in his final Ferrari season.

gilles_villeneuve.text: Villeneuve inherited the lead when Jarier’s Lotus retired, winning the first Grand Prix at Montreal for his first Formula One victory.
Villeneuve and Arnoux repeatedly touched wheels while fighting for second at Dijon; Villeneuve kept the place by less than a quarter of a second.
Starting second, Villeneuve took the lead when Jones hit a fuel feed problem, giving the turbocharged 126 CK victory in Monaco.
From seventh on the grid, Villeneuve led a five-car train at Jarama and won by 0.22 seconds. It was his final Grand Prix victory.

scheckter.text: Scheckter won from pole position and led all 76 laps, finishing 0.44 seconds ahead of Regazzoni’s Williams.
Scheckter won at Monza with Villeneuve second, sealing the drivers’ championship and the constructors’ title for Ferrari.
A year after winning the title, Scheckter failed to qualify the 312 T5 in Montreal.

mansell.text: On his Ferrari debut, Mansell won from sixth on the grid, the first Grand Prix victory for a car with a semi-automatic gearbox.
From 12th on the grid, Mansell passed Senna while they lapped Johansson’s Onyx, then won by nearly 26 seconds.
Mansell reversed in the pit lane, was black-flagged and then collided with Senna; he was disqualified and excluded from the next race.
From pole, Mansell lost places at the start but passed Senna after the stops and led when the race was stopped after 61 laps.

prost.text: Starting 13th, Prost worked through the field and passed Senna for the lead on lap 61 of 69 to win.
Prost passed Capelli’s Leyton House for the lead on lap 77 of 80, giving Ferrari its 100th Formula One victory.
Prost and Senna collided at the first corner and both retired, confirming Senna as champion with one race remaining.

raikkonen.text: Räikkönen won his first race for Ferrari, the opening round of the season, at Melbourne.
Third in the standings before the finale, Räikkönen won at Interlagos and took the title by one point from Hamilton and Alonso.
From sixth on the grid, Räikkönen passed Fisichella after a safety car restart and won, Ferrari’s only victory of 2009.
Räikkönen took the lead from Hamilton at the start in Austin and won, his first victory since the 2013 Australian Grand Prix.
